v.why: When edge 1->3 is absent, adding the 0->3 skip often restores the only path to the output (exps 19, 20), giving huge gains.
Removing edge 0->3 when edge 1->3 is already none can disconnect the output and collapse accuracy (exps 64, 65).
Without the 0->3 shortcut, edge 1->3 is a critical path to the output, so removing it hurts much more (exps 32, 33).
When edge 2->3 is absent, node 3 depends heavily on edge 1->3, so deleting it is far more damaging (exps 32, 34).
With edge 1->3 missing, adding a conv on 2->3 can reconnect a dead output and adds the main learnable path (exp 8).
If edge 0->2 is none, cutting 0->1 starves nodes 1 and 2 entirely, which hurts much more (exps 92, 93, 99).
Adding a conv where there was no edge adds a path and capacity, whereas replacing an existing conv_3x3 removes capacity (exp 77 vs 73).
Filling an absent 0->1 edge can activate a dead branch, while replacing an existing op only swaps one op for another (exp 30).
In skip-heavy cells with few learnable ops, the 0->3 identity shortcut dominates the cell, so removing it is less harmful or even helps (exp 62 vs 61).
Without an input-output shortcut on edge 3, a skip on 2->3 supplies the residual path that conv-heavy cells need (exps 81, 87 vs 82).

raw:
Most of these hypotheses rest on one structural fact: the output node (3) is fed only by edges 3, 4 and 5. When those paths are cut, accuracy collapses, so edits that cut or restore the last path to the output produce very large effects.

- **Last path cut:** edits that remove the only remaining input to node 3 collapse accuracy to chance. Examples are experiments 32, 64, 65 and 99.
- **Last path restored:** edits that reconnect a cut-off output recover 60–80 points on CIFAR-10. Examples are experiments 8, 19, 20, 30 and 77.
- **Cells made only of skip_connect or only of avg_pool:** these lack learnable convolutions. In them, removing the edge 0 → 3 skip actually helps (experiments 62 and 67). Adding a skip on edge 5 helps most when the cell has no edge 0 → 3 shortcut (experiments 81 and 87).
